comparator.name: Applied Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026-2027 appendix defines a 165-ECTS Applied Mathematics major and 15-ECTS minor. Year 1 is a compulsory 60-ECTS common Mathematics/Applied Mathematics foundation. The remaining 120 ECTS comprise 105 ECTS of major requirements and 15 ECTS of genuine minor space. First-year Project Applied Mathematics is used because it directly represents the named degree. For the two required project choices, Project Mathematical Modelling and Project Systems Theory are selected as the first two options in official order. Numerical Linear Algebra and Advanced Systems Theory are likewise the first two options in the required advanced-choice group. Statistical Modelling is the first Applied Mathematics elective not already used. These choices are fixed independently of UCR fit, and the open minor remains unpopulated.

programmes.label: Applied Mathematics at University of Groningen

exception.reason: The Groningen bachelor is a full disciplinary Applied Mathematics degree. Its 165-ECTS major builds from proof-based analysis, calculus, sets and numbers, graph theory, two linear-algebra courses, probability, programming, mechanics and linear systems into topology, complex and functional analysis, multivariable analysis, ordinary and partial differential equations, numerical analysis, optimization, mathematical modelling, computational science, advanced systems and modelling projects, and a 15-ECTS Applied Mathematics research project. UCR offers a useful six-course mathematics sequence plus programming, data science and selected computational applications, but it does not provide the breadth, depth or staged project and research spine required for a 24-course Applied Mathematics programme. A UCR programme assembled from mathematics, AI, data science and applications would be a coherent quantitative or computational pathway, not a defensible substitute for the target degree.
exception.curriculumContext: The current formal regulations account for exactly 180 ECTS: a compulsory 60-ECTS first year, 105 ECTS of second- and third-year major requirements, and 15 ECTS of open minor space. Restricted choices are instantiated coherently and independently of UCR fit. The public programme page corroborates the common first year, numerical mathematics and systems/control directions, modelling and simulation emphasis, and final research project.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods covers foundational calculus, complex numbers, differential equations and introductory linear algebra; DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics extend that base. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming supplies Python and computational problem-solving. The workbook also contains relevant content in DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISARIN211 Decision-making in AI, DISCOMP311 Algorithms & Data Structures, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA311 Neural Networks & Deep Learning and DISDATA312 Robotics. However, the available curriculum has no dedicated proof-based sequence in real analysis, metric and topological spaces, complex analysis and functional analysis; no full sequence in ordinary and partial differential equations; no graph theory, sets and numbers, advanced systems theory or multiple applied-mathematics modelling projects; and no equivalent 15-ECTS disciplinary research project. Several especially relevant courses, including DISMATH213, DISMATH312 and DISDATA312, have no planned term for the Fall 2026 cohort in the authoritative workbook. These gaps prevent an academically honest 24-course Applied Mathematics closest match.
